faq.description: Find answers to common questions about hiring {roles}, engagement models, communication, technology and project delivery.

items.question: Can I hire a dedicated {role}?
items.answer: Yes. With the dedicated developer model, your {role} focuses on your project and works as an extension of your existing team, following your priorities, tools and communication rhythm.

items.question: Can I hire a complete {short} development team?
items.answer: Yes. A dedicated development team can be structured around your project requirements, combining {roles} with supporting roles such as backend development, QA, UI/UX or project coordination where applicable.

items.question: Can your {roles} work with our existing team?
items.answer: Yes. Developers can join your existing workflow: communicating through your team's chat and meeting tools, working in your project-management system and contributing through your code repositories, with code review and testing as part of the process.

items.question: Can {roles} work with teams in different time zones?
items.answer: Yes. Communication and working-hour overlap can be structured around your team's working hours and project requirements, so there is regular time for meetings, reviews and collaboration.

items.question: Can I sign an NDA before discussing my project?
items.answer: Yes. Confidentiality arrangements, including an NDA, can be put in place when required before you share project details. Let us know your requirements when you get in touch.

items.question: Who owns the source code and intellectual property?
items.answer: Ownership of the source code and intellectual property is defined in the engagement agreement and project-specific terms, so it is clear for your project from the start.

items.question: How quickly can I onboard {roles}?
items.answer: It depends on the expertise you need, developer availability and your project requirements. Once we understand your needs, we can share expected availability and an onboarding plan.

items.question: Can I scale the development team later?
items.answer: Yes. The engagement can be adjusted as your project requirements evolve, for example by adding developers or other specialists, subject to developer and team availability.

finalCta.description: Share your requirements and we'll help you find the right {roles} for your product, timeline and engagement model.
